text: Hello everyone, welcome to Joey's class.In today's lesson, we are going to learn how to show different emotions by using stress and intonation.Besides, we are going to analyze the emotions of some cartoon characters by identifying their facial expressions.First, let's listen and answer the following question.How did the kidnappers sound?Why do we always get the boring jobs?Shut up and listen.Kitty, please.The kidnapper in brown sounded bored and dissatisfied.The kidnapper in green sounded rude and impatient.Thank you, Kitty.I agree with you.And we can find.The first sentence is said with stresses on the words why, we, boring.The other sentence is said with stresses on the phrase shut up and the word listen.In spoken English, when the speakers want to show emotions, they can put stress on the word they wish to emphasize.Let's practice.Listen to the sentences and tell the speaker's emotions.While listening, please pay attention to the stressed words.1Oh no, I'm afraid of spiders.2I'm afraid of spiders.2I'm well prepared.I can win the match.3Jim has been very ill recently.I hope he will feel better soon.Let's check.3APlease listen again and identify the stressed words in the following sentences.听录音,识别中毒的单词。Each sentence will be read twice.The first sentence is said with stresses on the wordsNo and afraid.The stressed word in the second sentence is win.In the last sentence, the speaker puts stresses on the words very ill.It's time for you to practice.Read the following sentences after me.Let's move on and learn more about stress.When we are speaking English, the words with stress can change the underlying meaning of a sentence.If we put the stress on the word I, the sentence may meanSomebody else might think Ben will win the match.What about putting the stress on the word don't?It meansIn my opinion, Ben won't win the match.And if we lay the stress on Ben, the sentence meansI think someone else will win the match.As you can see, we can express different meanings by stressing different words in the same sentence.Now it's your turn.Read the sentences aloud, stressing the words in red.I don't think Ben will win the match.Actually, different intonation patterns can also help us show different meanings.不同的语调也可以帮助我们表达不同的意思。In fact, different intonation patterns can also help us show different meanings.Listen and think about what Ben means by using different intonations.In the first dialogue, Ben used rising intonation.Maybe Ben didn't hear Alice or didn't hear her clearly.In the second dialogue, Ben used falling intonation.Maybe Ben can't offer help at the moment.We can also use rising and falling intonation to show different emotions.我们也可以使用升降调来表达不同的情绪。In grade 8, we learned.Sometimes we make our voices rise at the end of sentences to express surprise or other feelings such as happiness.We also make our voices rise to show politeness.Listen and tell what emotion the speaker showed us in each sentence.Have I really won the competition?The speaker used rising intonation at the end of the sentence, and she sounded surprised.Don't be afraid.I won't let these dogs bite you.This time, the speaker used falling intonation at the end of the sentences, and she sounded brave.I've studied for ten hours already.I wish I could watch some TV.The speaker used falling intonation at the end of the sentences to show she was bored.Let's have a brief summary.We usually use rising intonation to show high-energy emotions like happiness, surprise, fright, and annoyance.We often use falling intonation to show boredom, bravery, confidence, and disinterest.Please read the sentences after the recording.To show the emotions correctly, you should put stress on the words in bold, and pay attention to the intonations.Let's have
